newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-DUNDEE WINS RIGHT TO WEAR GERMAN SHIRT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-DUNDEE WINS RIGHT TO WEAR GERMAN SHIRT.

text.p: South African-born striker Sean Dundee has been granted German citizenship, clearing the way for him to play for the national soccer side, the Interior Ministry said on Tuesday.

Dundee, who plays for German club Karlsruhe and is the top goalscorer of the Bundesliga this season with 13 goals, applied for citizenship using a special fast-track method reserved for cases of "public interest".
The German Soccer Federation (DFB) supported his application and national coach Berti Vogts has expressed a strong interest in the 23-year-old Dundee, who has lived in Germany for four years.
His decision to apply for German citzenship sparked outrage in his native country where some politicians accused him of turning his back on South Africa and called for the move to be blocked.

The German Interior Ministry had to agree to the decision to grant him citizenship because the rules normally specify 10 years' residence. But the ministry said Dundee fulfilled the minimum conditions for naturalisation of sports stars, which were accepted as exceptional cases a year ago.
South Africa decided at the end of October to abandon efforts to persuade him to join their own World Cup squad.
The Durban-born forward spurned numerous call-ups from South Africa, who accused Vogts of poaching him and putting pressure on him to play for Germany instead of South Africa.
The player was also courted by Ireland manager Mick McCarthy earlier this year when it was learned that his grandparents were Irish.
Dundee, whose surname has inevitably earned him the nickname "Crocodile", is following a path well-trodden by foreign sports stars who have won German citizenship.
High-jumper Alina Astafei and promising tennis star Alex Radulescu both rejected their native Romania to become Germans in recent years.
